1.  The instant Appeal has been listed for passing appropriate order on the instant Interlocutory Application filed on behalf of appellant under Section 430 (1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence/grant of bail during the pendency of the instant Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 930 of 2019 in connection with G.R. (POCSO) No.3429 of 2017, (Govindpur P.S. Case No.101 of 2017) against the judgment of conviction dated 18.07.2019 and order of sentence dated 19.07.2019 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge- V-cum- Special Judge (POCSO), East Singhbhum, Jamshedpur whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and 4/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, (POCSO Act) and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs. 20,000/- for offence under Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) and in default of fine, the convict was directed to undergo further imprisonment of six months and by further holding that Bihari Lal Yadav Son Of Anil Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150827147/
1 there is no need to impose any further sentence separately for offence under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC and under Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act),
2.

sentences.text: It has been contended on behalf of the appellant that it is a case where the appellant has falsely implicated reason being that none of the witnesses have supported the prosecution version.

Further,
there is no incriminating material has been found during the trial even though the appellant has been convicted.

3. While on the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and has contended that the age of the victim female child is 07 years and the culpability of the present appellant has been corroborated even in the DNA profile.
4. As such, it is not a fit case where the sentence is to be suspended.
5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone through the impugned judgment as also the lower Court record which has been called for by the Court.
6. It is evident from the factual aspect that the female child who was having the age of about five and half years at the time of occurrence has been subjected to sexual assault.
7. The Investigating Agency has collected the evidence for the purpose of sending the same to the FSL as also for DNA.
The said report having been marked as exhibit-09/01 corroborates the occurrence.

8. This Court considering the aforesaid fact has found the prosecution version has been corroborated by all the prosecution witnesses as also the DNA and hence, it is not a fit case where the sentence is to be suspended.
9. Accordingly, IA No.10698 of 2024 is hereby rejected.

10. It is made clear that any observation made hereinabove will not prejudice the case on merit,
since, the criminal appeal is pending before this Court for its consideration.
(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Navneet Kumar, J.) Basant/S.Das 2 Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 930 of 2019 Bihari Lal Yadav Son Of Anil Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150827147/
